data.name: Rahmat
data.gender_notes: Rahmat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Rahmat is an Arabic name derived from the word 'rahmah' which means mercy or compassion. The name Rahmat carries the meaning “Mercy, Compassion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Rahmat usually hope their child will grow to embody mercy, compassion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Allah is referred to as 'Rahman' and 'Rahim', meaning the Most Merciful and the Most Compassionate. A person named Rahmat embodies these divine attributes and is expected to be kind, merciful and compassionate.
data.etymology: Rahmat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mercy, Compassion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rahmat total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

Muslims strive to embody these values in their daily lives, and the name Rahmat is a constant reminder of the significance of treating others with kindness and forgiveness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Rahmat holds deep significance as it reminds those who bear it of God's infinite mercy and compassion towards His creation. Muslims believe that God has bestowed His mercy on all of His creatures and that it is a divine attribute to be emulated. Additionally, the name Rahmat can serve as a reminder of the Day of Judgment when God's mercy and compassion towards His creation will be the ultimate Redeemer. Hence, the name Rahmat is more than just a label, it is a call to reflect God's attributes of mercy and compassion in one's actions, words, and thoughts.
